title: 9 ways to decrease your chance of bootstrapping a successful company
summary: Rob lists nine mistakes that lower a bootstrapper's odds, drawn from working with over 1,000 entrepreneurs. They include facing funded competitors, going horizontal, relying on one-time sales, going freemium, pricing too low, and marketing late. He argues bootstrappers die from running out of motivation, not money.

principles.text: Avoid head-to-head fights with funded competitors; pick a niche they can't afford to enter.
principles.quote: It’s not that you can’t beat funded competition. But taking them on head to head is like wrestling 2 weight classes above your own.

principles.text: Go vertical: niches are cheaper to reach, less contested, higher margin, and spread by word of mouth.
principles.quote: Niches are easier to penetrate, cheaper to advertise to, have less competition, higher profit margins, and word of mouth is a vibrant force.

principles.text: Build recurring revenue into the model rather than relying on one-time sales.
principles.quote: On the first day of every month you start with zero dollars in revenue, and you have to hustle like crazy to hit your number.

principles.text: Price up-market: low price points need customer volumes a bootstrapper can't reach.
principles.quote: These days I advise people to go up-market and try for $30/month and $50/month price points.

principles.text: Start marketing before the product is finished, for example by building an email list from a landing page.
principles.quote: Rumor has it that DropBox had 200,000 emails by the time they launched, based on driving a ton of traffic to a landing page with a single video

principles.text: Bootstrappers fail from lost motivation, so set realistic expectations about how long it takes.
principles.quote: So for you, stalwart bootstrapper, the number one cause of death is not running out of money, but running out of motivation.
